strings.name: Erling Haaland
strings.summary: Born in England and raised in Bryne, Haaland played for Molde, Salzburg and Dortmund before Manchester City. Known for positioning, strength and finishing, he scored a record 36 Premier League goals in 2022–2023 and helped City win the treble. He made his World Cup debut in 2026. His scoring also depends on teammates’ chances and tactics.
strings.influence.rationale: Broke the Premier League single-season scoring record and became a key attacker for leading European clubs.
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained in Bryne FK’s youth system before joining senior football.
strings.highlights.h1.title: 36-goal Premier League season
strings.highlights.h1.text: Scored 36 in 2022–2023, setting the competition’s single-season record.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Treble-winning team member
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped City win the Premier League, FA Cup and Champions League in 2023.
strings.timeline.t1.title: World Cup debut
strings.timeline.t1.text: Represented Norway at the 2026 World Cup, his first senior major tournament finals.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Contract through 2034
strings.timeline.t2.text: Signed a long-term Manchester City extension running until summer 2034.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Treble season
strings.timeline.t3.text: Helped City win the treble in his debut season and won the Premier League Golden Boot.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined Manchester City
strings.timeline.t4.text: Transferred from Dortmund to City, entering the Premier League.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Moved to Dortmund
strings.timeline.t5.text: Joined Dortmund, gaining Bundesliga and Champions League experience.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Salzburg spell
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined Salzburg, attracting wider attention through Champions League performances.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Bryne senior debut
strings.timeline.t7.text: Progressed from Bryne’s youth team to senior football, later moving to Molde.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Leeds
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born while his father played in England; moved to Norway in childhood.
